Something hungry.

Thomas would often goad Harry into interruptions: a jot of food for Voldemort, perhaps; but in that moment, he had spoken of something else entirely. “I’ve seen a book,” he whispered as the sun dipped behind the tower. “A light you can’t see, but you know it’s there.” Harry didn’t ask what he meant. It was the same one Christine Weasley had once mentioned, when she had sat by his bed and spoken of forgotten wisdom.

Inside, tucked beneath a folded map of the grounds, lay a single object: a moonshade feather, preserved between two sheets of parchment written in intricate, looping script:
